test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-idn-004/Biolog.Features.PersonLifecycle.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/quality.sh
summary: Implements BIO-IDN-004 (identity lifecycle and emergency suspension), including the full BIO-IDN-004-QA-01 resolution across five rounds. Extends BIO-IDN-002/003's narrow, read-only IPersonExistenceGateway pattern into a write-capable IPersonLifecycleGateway. AC01: LifecycleTransitionPolicy is a closed, explicit whitelist mirroring BIO-IDN-001's own baseline table. AC02/AC03/AC04 as previously implemented. QA-01's full history: round 1 (commit-then-publish) left a silent gap; the round-1 fix (publish-then-commit) was rejected in round 2 for emitting a false revocation on a routine rejected commit; the round-2 fix (commit-then-publish with an explicitly modelled pending state) was rejected in round 3 because the pending state was derived from current status and vanished on reactivation; the round-3 fix (a durable IPendingSuspensionReconciliationStore, independent of current status) was rejected in round 4 because the pending record was still marked AFTER the ordinary supplementary lifecycle audit write - an audit-sink outage aborted the method before the pending record was ever created, leaving the person SUSPENDED with no revocation event and no pending record to find. This round's fix: for a suspension, the pending record is marked the VERY FIRST thing after the gateway commit succeeds, before either the ordinary audit write or the revocation publish is even attempted; those two writes are then attempted independently of one another's outcome, with the revocation publish's own failure surfaced with priority since it is AC02's security-critical write. The durable-tracking design itself (the store, ReconcilePendingRevocationsAsync, HasPendingRevocationsAsync) is unchanged from round 3 - this fix is purely about the ordering of the two writes relative to the pending mark.
notes: Verified end-to-end across five rounds: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api clean (0 warnings/errors). 70/70 feature-local tests (2 new for round 5: a pending-record-survives-an-audit-sink-outage proof reproducing round 4's exact finding, and a proof that the audit write and revocation publish are genuinely independent attempts). Break-it-on-purpose verified for round 5: reverted the pending mark to after the audit write, confirmed the new regression test failed with audit_unavailable and no pending record - reproducing the exact reported finding - then restored and re-confirmed green (all four prior rounds' own break-it-on-purpose tests also re-verified passing against the current code). 70/70 dotnet integration tests (one unrelated pre-existing flaky ObservabilityTests failure confirmed non-deterministic and unrelated to this story - passes in isolation and on rerun; 160/160 dotnet unit tests unaffected). BIO-IDN-001 (70/70) feature-local regression unaffected. 59/59 offline structural checks (5 new QA-01 round-4/5 checks). contract-freeze PASS. traceability PASS. module-reference-direction PASS. Full scripts/quality.sh (repo-wide gate, same non---full mode every prior identity-wave story's evidence recorded): QUALITY: PASS, 0 failures.
